Not a training run -- a manifest cleanup pass, logged here to track dataset provenance over time. Found via manual spot-check (scripts/sample_alignment_check.py) that some LRCLIB-timestamped chunks were badly misaligned with their audio (one off by 16s). Root cause: dataset.py matched LRCLIB lyrics to audio by artist/title text only, no duration check -- a loose YouTube search can return a different edit/upload (wrong video entirely, looped upload, different single cut) whose lyrics text matches but whose timing doesn't. Confirmed via LRCLIB's duration field vs actual downloaded audio duration: 37/81 songs (46%) had a mismatch >5s, up to 647s (Tame Impala 'Dracula' turned out to be a 14-minute interview video, not the song). Dropped all 37. Also: added a 0.25s padding on chunk audio slicing (train.py) to stop clipping word onsets/codas at chunk boundaries, and a filter dropping near-empty/symbol-only segments like placeholder '♪' instrumental-break lines (42/3756 segments, some spanning 20+s). Added a forward-looking duration check in dataset.py (_download_billboard_audio) so future builds reject mismatched songs automatically instead of silently keeping them.
